bearerAuth.description: Keycloak access token issued for the horecaos-api audience

storefrontAppId.description: The registered app's id. An identifier, not a secret: it appears in a browser bundle by design. Sent alongside the customer's session, never instead of it.
storefrontAppId.name: X-Storefront-App-Id

storefrontAppSecret.description: A confidential client's secret. Server-side only; a public client has none and must not send one.
storefrontAppSecret.name: X-Storefront-App-Secret

info.description:
The HorecaOS storefront contract: the one API every storefront is built against, ours and a vendor's alike. The core does not change per storefront.

## Which storefront is asking

Every request names the app that is asking, in addition to the customer's own session and never instead of it: the app says which storefront, the session says which customer. Send the app's id in `X-Storefront-App-Id`. Anonymous browsing stays anonymous for the customer, and requires an app identity all the same, so the platform can meter, rate-limit and revoke.

Rollout: the header is accepted and checked now, and a request without it still works while the platform counts how many arrive unattributed. It becomes required, with notice under the deprecation policy below, once that count has stayed at zero.

## Public and confidential clients

A **public client** is a browser-only storefront. It holds no secret, because a browser keeps none: it registers an app id and an origin allowlist, and the platform checks each request's `Origin` against that list. It is attributable and revocable. It is **not authenticated**, in the sense a browser cannot deliver, and nothing in this contract says otherwise.

A **confidential client** is a server-backed storefront. It registers a secret, sent in `X-Storefront-App-Secret`, and gets what that earns: higher quotas and access to any endpoint judged unsafe for a public client. Never put that secret in a browser bundle; a bundled secret is not one.

A tenant authorises an app for a brand and can revoke it. Revoking takes effect on the app's next request. A refused app is told which thing is wrong: `APP_UNREGISTERED`, `APP_SUSPENDED`, `APP_NOT_AUTHORISED`, `APP_REVOKED`, `APP_ORIGIN_MISMATCH`, `APP_SECRET_INVALID` or `APP_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`.

## What is promised

Each operation carries `x-horecaos-surface`. **`published`** operations are the guaranteed public surface: a published path is never removed within v1, and change is additive only. **`internal`** operations are channel-specific (the Telegram and dine-in QR routes) and may change without notice; do not build on them.

## Deprecation policy

A breaking change to a published path is a new major version served alongside the old one. The old version keeps working for at least **12 months** from the day the replacement is announced; an operation scheduled for removal is marked `deprecated` in this document from that day. Nothing in the published surface is removed inside `v1`.
info.title: HorecaOS Platform API

get.description: Not-found for an unclaimed hostname and for a claimed-but-unverified one alike -- ChannelSetupService#resolveHostname's own doc explains why an unverified custom domain must not resolve.
get.summary: The tenant and channel this hostname answers on

post.description: Scanning authorises nothing by itself. The printed token is exchanged once for a short-lived, table-scoped token, and that is what every subsequent call carries. Rotating the table's code revokes every token minted from it in the same transaction. Every failure — unknown, rotated, archived, branch not configured — answers identically, so a caller holding a guessed value learns nothing from the difference.
post.summary: Exchange a scanned table code for a guest token

post.description: A guest who has scanned a free table opens a provisional session -- a claim -- without waiting for staff (ADR 0143). It is an explicit action, never a side effect of scanning, and it needs both credentials a round does: the table's guest token (X-Dine-In-Token, the proof of where) and the customer's ordinary signed-in session (Authorization: Bearer, the proof of who). It never accepts a table, a location or a tenant. The claim becomes an ordinary session once a round the restaurant has accepted is on it, and lapses -- giving the table back to the room -- if nothing follows within its window. If somebody already sits at the table, the call answers with their session and created=false rather than a second one. Every reason the table cannot be taken (the branch has not turned this on, a booking holds the table, a cap is reached, the account is refused, the table is out of service) is one answer, 409 TABLE_NOT_AVAILABLE, with no reason.
post.summary: Seat yourself at a free table

get.description: The session id is checked against the table the guest's token was minted for, not merely parsed. A guest who edits it reaches nothing.
get.summary: The running bill at the guest's own table

post.description: Moves the session to BILL_REQUESTED, which is a request rather than a payment: nothing is captured here, and a party that then orders one more round moves it back.
post.summary: Ask for the bill

post.description: A cart bound to the table (PUT .../carts/{cartId}/table) is put on this bill by checkout itself, in the transaction that creates the order, and needs no call here. This is the attach for a cart that was never bound: the order was already priced, reserved and confirmed by the ordinary checkout, and this only records that it belongs to this table's evening -- the exact write TableSessionController's operator endpoint makes, reached here through the guest's own token instead of a capability. Calling it twice with the same order is not an error: the second call finds the order already on this bill and answers with the bill unchanged. The guest token alone proves the caller is at this table, not that the order named in the body is theirs, so this also requires the ordinary signed-in session (Authorization: Bearer) the checkout that created the order was placed under -- see requireOwnOrder's own doc.
post.summary: Attach a just-placed order to the table's bill

get.description: The same answer as the operations surface, readable before an account exists, for the storefronts' and the mobile app's own clients.
get.summary: The platform's languages (storefront)

get.description: The balance, what is spendable today, what an unfinished checkout is holding, and the next lot to expire. Points are not money: they cannot be withdrawn, cannot be transferred, and have no value outside the platform.
get.summary: One points balance

get.description: Every entry that produced the balance, newest first, each with the balance it left behind. This is what a disputed figure is answered from.
get.summary: The movements behind a balance

post.description: Returns at most twenty active pickup branches, nearest first. Each result carries the same current serviceability answer the checkout path will later re-resolve authoritatively. POST so the caller's coordinate travels in the body rather than the query string; nothing is written and no resource is created.
post.summary: Find the nearest pickup locations with a published storefront menu

get.description: No installation, no binding, or a suspended one: every field is null, which the storefront reads as 'inject nothing'. Cacheable — these values change only when an operator reconfigures analytics, never per request.
get.summary: This brand's analytics installs, for client-side injection

post.description: Public. Answers 202 whether or not the token names a live link of this brand (unknown, archived, expired and other-brand tokens count nothing and say nothing), so the endpoint cannot be used to probe which tokens exist. Records no address, user agent or cookie. Non-idempotent by design: each open is one click. Limited per token and visitor.
post.summary: Count one open of an attribution link

post.description: The cart is bound to this location and channel for its whole life. Moving location rebuilds it, because catalog, availability, tax, fee and promise all change with the branch.
post.summary: Open a cart at one location

get.description: Scoped to the caller's own account. A cart id is not a bearer token: knowing one does not read the basket it belongs to.
get.summary: Read a cart

get.description: Answers with the caller's own address id and never with the address. The doorstep is personal data and is read from ADR 0015's own endpoint, where the decrypt is recorded against a purpose. A sub-resource rather than a field on the cart, so reading a basket stays one query and a cart response can never grow a field that is somebody's home.
get.summary: Which saved address this cart is going to

put.description: Names one of the caller's own saved addresses, never an address typed into this request: ADR 0015 owns what an address is, including whether it has a coordinate and why. The chosen address is copied on to the cart, so editing or archiving it afterwards cannot change where an order in flight goes. Clears any attached quote, because ADR 0037 prices delivery from the destination and a basket priced to one door is not priced to another.
put.summary: Say where a delivery cart is going

put.description: Clears any attached quote in the same statement that bumps the cart version. A cart holding a price for contents it no longer has is the shortest path to charging for a basket nobody agreed to.

post.description: Returns a new cart with the same lines and no price. The old cart is abandoned: ADR 0019 never carries a cart across locations, because the prices shown would be prices that do not apply.
post.summary: Rebuild this cart at another location

put.description: ADR 0140. The method is an input to the price whenever a promotion reads it ("5% off when paying by Click"), so it is stored on the cart before pricing, and clears any attached quote the same way a line edit does. A null code clears the selection, and an unselected method never earns a payment-method promotion. Checkout with a different method than the cart was priced with is refused PRICE_CHANGED when such a promotion exists, which is the re-quote the customer app has to design around.
put.summary: Select how the cart will be paid

get.description: Only methods that would actually work: the channel offers them here, this build implements them, a customer may choose them, and a merchant account resolves for this branch today. A method whose provider binding is suspended is absent rather than listed and refused, because an unusable method offered to a customer is a checkout that fails at its last step. The codes map to customer wording in the storefront, the way a serviceability reason does.
get.summary: What this cart may be paid with

post.description: Returns the total and a context hash valid for 15 minutes. Checkout accepts only this quote for this cart, so a client cannot present a quote priced for a different, cheaper basket.
post.summary: Price the cart and bind the quote to it

delete.description: Does nothing when none is applied. Clears any attached quote, the same as applying one does.
delete.summary: Remove the cart's applied promo code

post.description: ADR 0072. Checked read-only against live coupon state before it is stored — active, in its window, and not exhausted — and checked again, independently, on every subsequent price. A cart already carrying a code has it replaced rather than refused: this platform supports at most one applied code per cart. Clears any attached quote, because a code changes what the total will be.
post.summary: Apply a promo code to the cart

put.description: ADR 0047's cart-to-table binding. The table is read from the guest's dine-in token (X-Dine-In-Token), never from the request: a body that named its own table would be a claim a client could edit to reach the next table's bill. Checkout then asks for the same token again (the binding is remembered state, so the guest is re-proved), refuses the order if nobody is seated and otherwise puts it on the table's bill in the same transaction that creates it, so the round cannot be lost between two requests. Clears any attached quote, because a bound cart is another cart; re-price before checkout.
put.summary: Bind a dine-in cart to the table the guest scanned

post.description: Idempotent under the tenant-scoped Idempotency-Key. Repeating the request returns the same order; a settled business rejection returns the same rejection rather than running again against a changed cart. A cart bound to a table (ADR 0047) also needs the guest's live dine-in token (X-Dine-In-Token) at the table it is bound to: the binding is remembered state, and the order goes on the bill of whoever sits there now, so the guest is re-proved at checkout. Without it the answer is a conflict (reason TABLE_TOKEN_REQUIRED, TABLE_TOKEN_ENDED or TABLE_BINDING_STALE).
post.summary: Turn a priced cart into an order

get.description: A listing only. A vacancy carries one outbound contact the tenant chose to publish (a phone number, an e-mail address, a Telegram or web address) and nothing of a candidate: the platform has no application form and stores no applicant data.
get.summary: A brand's published vacancies, newest first
One vacancy, with its branch and its one contact

post.description: A batch of at most 20 {itemId, revisionNo, event}, event one of IMPRESSION, CLICK, DISMISSAL (a pop-up) and COMPLETION (a story). Counted per item, revision, tenant day and channel; no identifier of any kind is stored. Client-reported and labelled so: anyone can inflate them, and they are not a metric the reporting layer consumes. An event naming an item or revision the brand does not have, or one that makes no sense for the kind, is rejected and counted and the rest of the batch is kept.
post.summary: Report anonymous view counts

get.description: News, gallery, recipes and vacancies, each true only while the tenant's plan includes the editorial tier and the brand has turned the kind on. All false when it has not; an unknown brand is a 404.
get.summary: Which editorial kinds a brand runs
A brand's published gallery albums, newest first
One gallery album with its images

get.description: Banners and promo cards in the carousel, product groups, and from later releases stories, a promo grid and a pop-up, in order, with ready-made image rendition URLs. `channel` is the tenant's channel code, as the menu read takes it; `locale` is a BCP 47 tag, a bare `uz` read as `uz-Latn`. A text the visitor's language lacks is served in the brand's default and `textLocale` says which. The same for every visitor; an unknown brand, a brand of another tenant and an unknown channel are one 404.
get.summary: The home content of a brand on a channel
A brand's published news, newest first
One news article, its body as typed blocks
A brand's published recipes, newest first
One recipe, its body as typed blocks

get.description: Anonymous and cached for a minute. enabled is false, with no tags, while the tenant's feedback settings are off. Otherwise the active tags, split by sentiment (at most eight each, in the tenant's order), each with its wording in every locale and its icon. The storefront shows the positive tags for 4-5 stars, the negative for 1-2 and both for 3, and at most maxTagsPerReview may be sent. publicComments is true only when the brand shows comments publicly, which is when the consent box means anything; consentTextKey names the storefront's own translated sentence.
get.summary: The feedback tags a customer is offered, and whether to show the public-display box

post.description: Candidates best first, each with a point, normalized components, the provider's reference, a confidence, a precision and when it was calculated. A result outside the region's box is LOW_CONFIDENCE whatever the provider claimed. A result is a suggestion the customer confirms on a map; nothing here is stored, and nothing here can produce a GEOCODER point.
post.summary: Find the places an address names

post.description: The result is absent when the provider knows nothing there. The same region constraint and the same LOW_CONFIDENCE rule as a forward lookup.
post.summary: Name what is at a point

post.description: Non-mutating; a POST only because the address text must stay out of the URL. Constrained to the tenant's region, ranked toward `near`. A provider that is not configured or is down answers 200 with status UNAVAILABLE, never an exception. Rate limited per customer and per tenant; answers are cached per tenant for the provider licence's limit.
post.summary: Type-ahead completions for a half-typed address

post.description: The identity comes from the caller's own token — issuer and subject, never a phone number, because a recycled number would otherwise hand one person another's order history. The grant is single-use and is only honoured at the brand it was proved for.
post.summary: Turn a verified number and a token into a customer account

post.description: The step that was missing. Redeems a single-use grant, finds or creates the account the proven number belongs to, and returns an opaque bearer the storefront presents on every later call. Unauthenticated, because a customer signing in for the first time has nothing to authenticate with — the grant is the authorisation, and it is spent here.
post.summary: Turn a proven number into a session

delete.description: Ends the session the caller is holding, and only that one. The session is named by the token in the Authorization header rather than by an id in the path, so there is nothing to edit in order to end somebody else's. Tapping it twice is not an error.

post.description: Answers the same way whether or not the number already has an account: nothing on this path reads the customer tables, so it cannot leak what it never looks at. Limited per number in the database and per caller in memory, and a new challenge retires any earlier one for the same number.
post.summary: Ask for a one-time code

post.description: Costs one of the challenge's attempts however it turns out. A wrong code says how many attempts are left; an unknown, expired, superseded, exhausted or already-used challenge all answer identically. Success returns a single-use grant, which is proof of the number and not a session. POST /sessions is what exchanges it for one (ADR 0051).
post.summary: Submit a code

get.description: The brand's supported set (tenant.brand_locales), its own default first, then the platform's order. A brand that has chosen none answers with every language live in the registry's content tier, and says so (configured=false). A language the registry no longer has live is left out. Cacheable: it changes only when an operator edits the brand's languages.
get.summary: The languages this brand serves, default first

post.description: Returns one fee, or one stable refusal code and no fee. An address outside every zone of this branch is refused here and never re-homed to a branch that does cover it: substituting one changes the menu, the prices, the preparation time and eventually the legal entity on the receipt.
post.summary: Resolve the delivery fee for one point

get.description: One row per uz.horecaos.platform.tenancy.api.FulfillmentMode value. "sold" is whether the channel carries the mode at all, structurally, independent of the clock; "serviceable" is whether an order may be placed for it right now. A mode can be sold and not serviceable (outside hours, manually closed, at capacity, ...); it is never serviceable without being sold. "reason" is absent exactly when serviceable is true.
get.summary: Which fulfilment modes a channel sells at a location, and which are usable now

get.description: Reads the active publication and applies the location's current availability on top. A variant the location does not offer is absent; one it has run out of is present and not orderable. The channel is required and supplies both the publication and the price plane (ADR 0036): a menu priced against another channel is a menu whose prices change at checkout.
get.summary: The live menu for one location

get.description: Only fields the tenant already publishes on this branch elsewhere -- the same name and address shown in pickup search and printed on a receipt. Not found for an unknown, inactive, or cross-tenant location id.
get.summary: A branch's own published display name and address

get.description: One resolver, one stable reason code, and a next-available instant where one is computable. "Closed now" and "cannot pre-order" are different facts and are reported separately.
get.summary: Resolve serviceability for a channel and fulfilment mode

get.description: Names the provider, its public, referrer-restricted browser key (delivered here so it can be rotated without rebuilding or redeploying a storefront), the features on offer (TILES, SUGGEST, GEOCODE, REVERSE) and the provider's attribution text. `configured: false` means no map provider is set up in this environment: the screen must say so and let the customer type an address, never show an empty map. The server key is never in this response and is not representable in it. For a signed-in customer of this brand; a guest is not found.
get.summary: What this environment's map is, and whether it works

get.description: Includes the account id, which is otherwise unlearnable from the storefront, and the scope the profile is shared at. Contact points are listed by type and verification state and never by value.
get.summary: The caller's own account and profile

patch.description: The three fields a customer owns. Status, identity partition, merge target and policy version are not among them: each decides something about the account, and none is the account holder's to set. Under TENANT_SHARED the change is visible at every brand of the tenant, which is what profileScope says.
patch.summary: Change the caller's own display name, language, or timezone

get.description: Decrypted, because the person they belong to is asking, and the reveal is recorded against a purpose that says so. Archived addresses are not listed.
get.summary: The caller's own saved addresses

post.description: The coordinate source is required and must agree with the coordinates: an address awaiting geocoding and one that legitimately has no point — a mahalla house given by its ориентир — are different states, and only one is worth retrying. A customer may claim CUSTOMER_PIN, NOT_GEOCODED or LANDMARK_ONLY; the operator and geocoder sources are not theirs to assert.
post.summary: Save a new address

delete.description: Archived rather than deleted. The row is what a dispute about where an order went is answered from, and nothing depends on it staying readable to the customer: a cart and an order each hold their own copy, taken when the address was chosen, so an order in flight is unaffected. This is not an erasure request, which is a governed act over the whole account.
delete.summary: Remove one of the caller's own addresses

get.description: Not found for an address that is somebody else's, is archived, or never existed. The three are one answer, because telling them apart is how an address id becomes probeable.
get.summary: One of the caller's own saved addresses

put.description: The whole address, never a field of it: the lines live inside one encrypted document, and the coordinate and its source have to move together. Requires If-Match, so a second tab loses loudly.
put.summary: Replace one of the caller's own addresses

post.description: Creates one lead in the call centre's queue, linked to the caller's own account. 202: what was created is a work item for a person, not a call. The number to ring is in the body. A guest asking on behalf of a company says so with forCompany=true, which files it as a catering enquiry.
post.summary: Ask the restaurant to call me back

get.description: The outstanding PENDING request if there is one, else the most recent one of any status. 204 when the caller has never raised one.
get.summary: The caller's own current erasure request, if any

post.description: Records the request; it does not erase anything by itself (ADR 0029, ADR 0044). Execution is a separate, staff-performed act, because a real erasure has to be checked against things this endpoint does not decide on its own — an open dispute, a pending delivery, a legal hold. Idempotent: calling this again while a request is already outstanding, or after one already completed, returns that request rather than raising a duplicate.
post.summary: Ask to be forgotten

post.description: Idempotent for a request already cancelled. Refused for one that already completed — there is no undoing an erasure that already happened.
post.summary: Withdraw the caller's own PENDING erasure request

get.description: Product ids, most recently marked first. Ids and not menu items: the storefront already holds the published menu and resolves them against it, which is also what drops a dish this branch has stopped serving instead of showing a card that cannot be ordered.
get.summary: The products this customer marked

delete.description: 204 whether or not it was marked. Removing what was never there is the state the customer asked for.

put.description: Idempotent: marking twice is one fact, so a double tap or a retried request is a no-op rather than an error. A product that is not this brand's is refused -- a stale menu in a customer's hand is an ordinary way to reach that.

get.description: Cursor-paginated per ADR 0031: pass the previous page's nextCursor, and a null nextCursor is the end. Every row is the caller's own — the account is a predicate of the query and there is no parameter that widens it — so this enumerates a customer's history and never a brand's. Carries what a list shows and nothing beneath it: no lines, no modifiers, no notes, no destination. Open one order to read those.

parameters.description: The nextCursor of the previous page
parameters.name: cursor

schema.description: The nextCursor of the previous page

get.summary: The caller's own orders at this brand, newest first

get.description: Scoped to the caller's account inside the query. A customer cannot read another customer's order by knowing its id.
get.summary: Read one of the caller's own orders

post.description: Refused once the order is confirmed: the payment, fiscal, POS and fulfilment consequences of that are owned by ADR 0039, and half-performing them would be worse than refusing.
post.summary: Cancel an order before it is confirmed

post.description: Returns a Click payment link or a Payme base64 checkout URL, and the attempt identity the provider's callback will carry. A customer who abandons the checkout and comes back is given the same attempt: a second one is refused by a unique index, because two payable links against one order is a double charge waiting for somebody to open both. Nothing here credits anything — both surfaces are unsigned, so the amount the platform enforces is the one it checks when the provider calls back.
post.summary: Open a payment attempt and get its checkout surface

get.description: A list, possibly empty: an order paid in cash has no receipt from a payment provider, and a card payment has none until the provider reports it. A Payme refund is a second receipt beside the first, and a split payment can settle on two paths, so the answer is always a list. Only receipts still in force are listed (a receipt that has been corrected or voided is replaced by the document that corrected it), and only an https link. The link is the one the customer was sent when the receipt was issued; nothing else about the receipt is returned, and the customer's account is a predicate of the check, so another customer's order and a missing one are both 404.
get.summary: The links to the receipts filed for one of the caller's own orders

get.description: ADR 0074. Resolves each line's stored variant and modifier ids against the menu as it stands now for this order's own location and channel, and answers READY, PARTIAL or UNAVAILABLE. A client shows its repeat button on the verdict rather than matching names against a menu it loaded separately. This is a read: apply it through the ordinary cart path, POST /carts then PUT /carts/{cartId}/lines/{lineKey} with the ids returned here, so a repeated basket is priced and checked out by the same code every other basket travels. The plan is a snapshot — a dish can be 86'd between reading it and rebuilding the cart, and pricing stays the authority that refuses.
get.summary: Whether this order can be ordered again, and with what

post.description: Refused with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND when the order is not the caller's own, UNPROCESSABLE_STATE when it has not reached COMPLETED yet, and RESOURCE_CONFLICT when it already has a review. tagIds are the tags the customer tapped: at most five, active, this tenant's, and matching the rating (positive for 4-5, negative for 1-2, either for 3); anything else is VALIDATION_FAILED. publicConsent is whether the customer ticked the box allowing their words on the restaurant's public page; it counts only with a comment. Both are ignored while the tenant's feedback settings are off. There is no endpoint to edit or withdraw a review once submitted (ADR 0071); only the public display of its comment can be withdrawn.
post.summary: Rate a completed order, once

get.description: Counts each returned banner against today's cap. A banner the customer closed, one past the daily cap, and one whose offer has left its validity window are not returned.
get.summary: The banners to show this customer now

post.summary: The customer closed a banner; it is not shown again

get.description: Mints the code on first read rather than requiring a separate create call — a customer's own code is a durable identity, not a resource with a creation step worth exposing.
get.summary: The caller's own referral code, and their own redemption if they used one

post.description: Refused when the code is the caller's own (self-referral), when this account has already redeemed a code (at most one, ever, per brand), or when the brand runs no referral program right now. Nothing is credited by this call itself: the reward fires later, on the caller's first order to reach COMPLETED.
post.summary: Redeem a friend's referral code

get.description: Cursor-paginated per ADR 0031: pass the previous page's nextCursor, and a null nextCursor is the end. Each row carries its tags and where its comment stands for the public page (publicDisplay.state, and the reason code when it is hidden).
get.summary: The caller's own reviews at this brand, newest first

get.description: The storefront's own rating prompt (ADR 0159, Decision 4): the caller's COMPLETED orders at this brand, newest first, that carry no review and were placed within the brand's inlineWindowDays (seven unless the rating-prompt policy says otherwise). Empty while the tenant's feedback settings are off, so the storefront shows exactly what it showed before.
get.summary: Completed orders the caller has not yet rated, still inside the prompt window

get.description: Anonymous, cached for a minute and evicted by every hide, withdrawal and erasure, rate limited. Empty unless the brand's public visibility is RATING_AND_COMMENTS. Each entry is a comment its author agreed to show and a moderator (or the brand's own setting) approved, with its rating, tags, the day it was written and the branch name: no name, no customer, no order number, no review id, no time of day. The cursor is opaque. A tenant cannot filter this list by rating, pin, reorder or feature a comment, or reply to one.
get.summary: The brand's published comments, newest first

get.description: Anonymous, cached for five minutes, rate limited. While the brand's public visibility is NONE, or it has fewer than its minimum count of reviews, ready is false and every figure is null. Otherwise the count, the average to one decimal and the five-bar distribution (index 0 is one star). The average counts every review of the brand, whatever became of its comment: a rating is not words.
get.summary: The brand's rating summary, or nothing but a flag

post.description: The customer's own withdrawal of the consent they gave (ADR 0159, Decision 6): records a WITHDRAWN decision, hides the comment for CUSTOMER_WITHDREW and cannot be reversed by a moderator. Refused with UNPROCESSABLE_STATE for a comment that was never shared or is already off the page. Touches nothing else: the rating, the comment the restaurant's staff see and any case stay as they were.
post.summary: Take a comment off the restaurant's public page

get.description: Categories in authored order, each with its published entries. Text resolves to the requested locale and falls back to any other published translation rather than to the authoring code. A brand with no published FAQ answers an empty list, which is a screen with no questions and not a failure.
get.summary: The brand's published FAQ

get.description: Published links in authored order. The platform is a checked vocabulary so a storefront can choose an icon from it, and the URL is constrained at the database to http(s), tel: and mailto:.
get.summary: Where a customer can reach this brand

delete.description: Retires the binding and its endpoint. Unlinking what was never linked is the state this call asked for, so it always succeeds.

get.summary: Whether this account currently has a linked Telegram chat

post.description: Open the returned link (or send "/start <code>" to the bot directly) to link this brand's bot to your account. The code expires shortly and is single-use; opening it links immediately, with no further confirmation.
post.summary: Mint a Telegram deep-link code

post.description: Verifies window.Telegram.WebApp.initData against the brand bot's own token (HMAC-SHA-256, Telegram's official construction) and links immediately — no /start, no code, no second round trip.
post.summary: Link via a verified Telegram Mini App session

post.description: Open the returned deep link (or send it to the bot as "/start <code>") to continue in Telegram. The code expires shortly and is single-use.
post.summary: Mint a Telegram sign-in code

get.description: PENDING until the bot's request_contact handshake redeems the code, then SIGNED_IN with a session bearer -- returned once, exactly as POST .../identity/sessions returns one, just arriving through a poll instead of a request/response round trip.
get.summary: Poll a Telegram sign-in code

get.description: The tenant's own published text when it has one for this language; otherwise the platform's brand-neutral default with brandName interpolated in. Cached briefly like the FAQ, because this changes on the order of weeks.
get.summary: The document in force right now, in the requested language

post.description: Always accepts whatever GET would answer right now for this locale — a client cannot name an older or newer version. Recorded through the same ADR 0015 consent store every other acceptance in the platform uses, so publishing a later version never rewrites what this call recorded.
post.summary: Record that the signed-in customer accepts the document currently in force

get.description: False for a customer who never accepted anything, and false again the day after a new version publishes for a customer who only ever accepted the one before it — the storefront reads this after sign-in to decide whether to ask.
get.summary: Whether the signed-in customer has accepted the version currently in force

get.description: Always the highest published version -- a client cannot ask for an older one. Not-found when this channel has never published this page, or has published it but not in the requested locale.
get.summary: One static page, in the requested language

get.description: The OG image, if set, is an asset id -- render it through StorefrontMediaController's /media/{assetId} redirect, the same path the menu already uses for product photos.
get.summary: This channel's SEO title/description and OG image

get.description: The same channel-aware check the storefront menu and the cart make, scoped to one variant. The channel is required and is the tenant's own channel code, as on the menu read (ADR 0141): the stops that cover that channel apply, and so does its channel type's stop threshold (gap map row 4.4c). A value that names no registered channel is read as a bare channel type (e.g. WEB), for which only the stops covering every channel apply.
get.summary: Whether a variant is orderable here, and its remaining quantity if tracked

get.description: 302 to a short-lived signed URL. Only a PUBLIC, displayable asset resolves; anything else is not found, and private, missing and unverified are one answer so an id cannot be probed. `variant` (thumb, w400, w800, w1600) asks for a rendition instead of the original (ADR 0157): the closed set the platform renders, never an arbitrary width. A rendition that has not rendered, or that this asset is not owed, is not found, like any other asset that cannot be served.
get.summary: Redirect to a published image
